headings.title: Creation and composition of public defender commission
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the seven-member Public Defender Commission appointed by the governor with senate consent, requiring four lawyers and party balance.

headings.title: Terms of office, vacancies, and reappointment
headings.reviewNote: Sets six-year commissioner terms, provides for filling unexpired vacancies by the governor, and authorizes commissioners to succeed themselves.

headings.title: Ex officio membership of state director
headings.reviewNote: Designates the state public defender director as a nonvoting ex officio commission member who participates in all meetings except discussions of term renewal, removal from office, and other matters designated by the commission.

headings.title: Regular meetings and election of chairperson
headings.reviewNote: Mandates regular commission meetings presided over by a chairperson elected by commission members.

headings.title: Expense reimbursement for commission members
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits salaries for commission members while providing that they shall receive actual and necessary expenses incurred in performing their duties.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsection headings for 600.015 covering commission creation, six-year terms after April 1, 1982, director ex officio status, regular meetings, and expense reimbursement (L. 1972 H.B. 1314 § 2, A.L. 1976 H.B. 1095, A.L. 1982 H.B. 1169; effective 4-01-82).

headings.title: Creation of office of state public defender
headings.reviewNote: Creates the Office of State Public Defender as an independent department within the judicial branch.

headings.title: Appointment and qualifications of state director
headings.reviewNote: Directs commission appointment of the state director, supreme court oath, and required criminal defense and administrative qualifications.

headings.title: Full-time service, term, renewal, and removal
headings.reviewNote: Requires full-time service without outside law practice, establishes a four-year renewable term, and allows removal for good cause after notice and hearing.

headings.title: Compensation limit for state director
headings.reviewNote: Directs the commission to set the director's salary, not to exceed that of a circuit judge.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsection headings for 600.019 covering office creation within the judicial branch, director appointment and qualifications, full-time service, four-year renewable term and removal, and salary cap (L. 1982 H.B. 1169; effective 4-01-82).

headings.title: Employment and terms of defender personnel
headings.reviewNote: Directs the commission to employ public defenders for four-year terms (who may be reappointed) and directs public defenders to employ assistants, deputies, investigators, and other staff serving at pleasure, with holdover continuity for defenders in office on April 1, 1982.

headings.title: Licensing requirements and outside practice restrictions
headings.reviewNote: Requires public defenders, assistant public defenders, and deputy public defenders to be licensed Missouri attorneys, restricts outside law practice except as authorized by chapter 600 or commission rule, and permits full- or part-time employment.

headings.title: Compensation authority of the commission
headings.reviewNote: Requires the commission to fix the compensation of persons appointed under this section.

headings.title: Establishment of local and regional offices
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the commission to establish local and regional defender offices necessary to carry out statutory duties.

headings.title: Appointment and compensation of other system personnel
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the commission, on recommendation of the director, to appoint and fix the compensation of all other personnel necessary to the operation of the state public defender system.

headings.title: Contracts with private attorneys for defense services
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the commission to contract with private attorneys to provide defense services in such areas of the state and on such terms as it deems appropriate.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 subsection headings for 600.021 (rewrote shifted subsections 5 and 6 to match source text) covering defender employment and terms, licensing and outside practice limits, compensation, local or regional offices, other personnel appointments, and private attorney contracts (L. 1982 H.B. 1169, A.L. 1986 S.B. 451).

headings.title: Office space, utilities, and expense allocation
headings.reviewNote: Requires cities or counties to provide office space and utilities other than telephone service, allocating costs pro rata across multi-county districts, with state funding other expenses.

headings.title: Annual budget appropriation and submission procedure
headings.reviewNote: Establishes annual appropriation budgeting and directs direct submission to the governor and general assembly without alteration by the judicial department.

headings.title: State employees' retirement system membership benefits
headings.reviewNote: Entitles any public defender or employee of a public defender to all benefits of the Missouri state employees' retirement system under sections 104.310 to 104.550 (source footnote notes section 104.310 was repealed by H.B. 1643, et al., 1988).

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 600.040 covering city and county office space and utility obligations, annual appropriation budgeting without judicial alteration, and MOSERS retirement benefits (L. 1972 H.B. 1314 § 7, A.L. 1982 H.B. 1169, A.L. 2013 H.B. 215; footnote notes section 104.310 was repealed in 1988).

headings.title: Administrative and operational duties of state director
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates administrative responsibilities of the director including personnel supervision, annual reporting, office establishment, rulemaking, grants, training, and contracts.

headings.title: Rulemaking effectiveness under section 536.024
headings.reviewNote: Provides that no rule or portion of a rule promulgated under chapter 600 becomes effective unless promulgated pursuant to section 536.024.

headings.title: Acceptance of requests and discretionary legal services
headings.reviewNote: Directs the director and defenders, within commission guidelines and subsection 4, to accept requests from eligible persons entitled to counsel under chapter 600 or federal or state constitution or laws and provide legal services when appropriate in their discretion.

headings.title: Mandatory categories of required legal representation
headings.reviewNote: Requires legal services for eligible persons in six categories—felonies, misdemeanors with probable jail confinement unless waived, certain probation violations under section 559.036, sexually violent predator custody/appeals/release under section 632.489, constitutionally required appointments, and loss-of-liberty cases—while excluding county or municipal ordinance violations and other misdemeanors.

headings.title: Director delegation to bar members and representatives
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to delegate legal representation of an eligible person to any member of the state bar of Missouri and to designate representatives to make indigency determinations and assign counsel.

headings.title: Public Defender - Federal and Other Fund
headings.reviewNote: Creates the Public Defender - Federal and Other Fund in the state treasury to fund local public defender offices from appropriations, grants, gifts, donations, and bequests, with state treasurer custody, interest retention, and exemption from section 33.080 general revenue transfer.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 subsection headings for 600.042 (rewrote shifted/fabricated subsections 2 through 6 to match source text) covering director duties, section 536.024 rulemaking effectiveness, discretionary legal services, mandatory representation categories, director delegation authority, and the Public Defender - Federal and Other Fund (L. 1982 H.B. 1169 through A.L. 2024 S.B. 754, et al.).

headings.title: Conspicuous posting of right to counsel notice
headings.reviewNote: Requires detention facility custodians to post conspicuous notices detailing the right to appointed counsel, indigency criteria, potential cost liability, and contact details.

headings.title: Request for counsel and affidavit requirements
headings.reviewNote: Permits charged, detained, or unrepresented persons (or others on their behalf) to request state representation, requiring notice review, a section 600.086 affidavit upon renewal, and oral advisement of the punishment for intentionally falsifying the affidavit.

headings.title: Private consultation facilities in custodial detention
headings.reviewNote: Obligates detention facility custodians to provide private rooms for confidential consultation between detained individuals and defense counsel or representatives.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 600.048 covering conspicuous custodial right-to-counsel notices, counsel request and indigency affidavit procedures, and private consultation room duties (L. 1982 H.B. 1169, A.L. 2013 H.B. 215).

headings.title: Judicial determination and written waiver of counsel
headings.reviewNote: Permits waiver of counsel in potential confinement cases only upon judicial determination of knowing and intelligent waiver and execution of a signed written form containing mandatory statutory advisements.

headings.title: Probation waivers and mandatory findings before confinement
headings.reviewNote: Requires the waiver procedure before orders of probation, parole, or suspended sentence carrying possible confinement, and mandates three judicial determinations after a guilty plea or finding of guilty before imposing confinement.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 600.051 (refined subsection 2 title/note) covering written waiver of counsel requirements and mandatory judicial findings before imposing confinement, probation, parole, or suspended sentence (L. 1976 H.B. 1095 § 600.046).

headings.title: Motion requesting conference on individual defender caseload
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes district defenders with director or commission approval to move for a caseload conference involving individual defenders (not the entire office) and requires the clerk to immediately provide a copy to the prosecutor.

headings.title: Scheduling and notice of caseload conference
headings.reviewNote: Directs the presiding judge upon approval to schedule a conference within thirty days and provide notice to the defender and prosecutor.

headings.title: Judicial findings and authorized types of caseload relief
headings.reviewNote: Requires an order within thirty days and authorizes six specific forms of caseload relief, including appointing private counsel, modifying release conditions, and case waiting lists.

headings.title: Expedited appellate review of caseload relief order
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the prosecutor and district defender to seek expedited appellate review within ten days of the court's order.

headings.title: Preservation of other relief and post-conviction exclusion
headings.reviewNote: Preserves other legal remedies and specifies that caseload relief provisions cannot serve as grounds for post-conviction relief claims.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority and nonseverability under chapter 536
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes commission and supreme court rulemaking, subjecting commission rules to chapter 536 and section 536.028 with a nonseverability clause invalidating rulemaking authority and rules proposed or adopted after August 28, 2013 if legislative review powers are held unconstitutional.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 subsection headings for 600.063 covering individual defender caseload conference motions, 30-day scheduling, 30-day order and six forms of relief, 10-day expedited appellate review, post-conviction claim exclusion, and nonseverable chapter 536 rulemaking (L. 2013 H.B. 215).

headings.title: Judicial standards for appointing private defense counsel
headings.reviewNote: Requires a circuit judge before appointing private counsel to verify the defendant's financial status, provide a requested evidentiary hearing on undue hardship considering livelihood and involuntary servitude, and determine whether counsel possesses necessary criminal defense experience, education, and expertise.

headings.title: Prohibition against advancing personal litigation funds
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits judges from requiring appointed private attorneys to advance personal funds for client litigation expenses.

headings.title: Postponement or substitution for legislative employees
headings.reviewNote: Requires the appointing judge to postpone proceedings or appoint substitute counsel when an appointed lawyer is a general assembly employee during January 1 to June 1, veto or special sessions, or out-of-session committee hearings.

headings.title: Reimbursement of preapproved litigation expenses
headings.reviewNote: Permits appointed private counsel to seek payment from the public defender system for non-fee litigation expenses approved in advance by the director as reasonably necessary.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsection headings for 600.064 (corrected subsection 1 note) covering pre-appointment judicial duties, bar on advancing personal funds, postponement or substitution for general assembly employees, and preapproved litigation expenses (L. 2013 H.B. 215).

headings.title: Determination of indigency and eligibility standards
headings.reviewNote: Defines eligibility criteria for public defender services based on income, dependents, bond capacity, and inability to obtain private counsel.

headings.title: Commission rulemaking on indigency criteria
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the commission to promulgate and enforce rules governing indigency determinations by courts and public defenders.

headings.title: Indigency determination procedure and court review
headings.reviewNote: Governs initial eligibility assessments by defenders, judicial review upon party motion, termination of services upon non-indigency findings, and required factual affidavits.

headings.title: Penalty for intentional falsification of affidavit
headings.reviewNote: Designates intentional falsification of an indigency affidavit to obtain defender services as a class A misdemeanor.

headings.title: Financial status investigations and records access
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes defenders to investigate applicant financial status, require written information releases, and access state and local agency records without fee.

headings.title: Burden of proof on defendant to establish eligibility
headings.reviewNote: Places the legal burden of establishing financial eligibility for public defender services on the accused person.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 subsection headings for 600.086 covering indigency eligibility standards, commission rulemaking, defender and court determination procedures, class A misdemeanor penalty for false affidavits, financial investigations and fee-free agency records, and defendant burden of proof (L. 1976 H.B. 1095 § 600.052, A.L. 1982 H.B. 1169, A.L. 1993 S.B. 180).

headings.title: Contribution orders and reimbursement schedules
headings.reviewNote: Requires limited cash contributions without substantial hardship as a condition of representation and reimbursement if the defendant becomes financially able, while providing that payment difficulty or failure shall not reduce or affect defender services.

headings.title: Creation, filing, and enforcement of defender liens
headings.reviewNote: Allows a lien on defendant property for reasonable defender service value—mandatory when exceeding $150 and permissive below $150—requiring notice filing within ten days after disposition, personal service, court approval as a judgment at law without filing fees, and prosecutor enforcement, compromise, or waiver with director concurrence.

headings.title: Contracts with private collection attorneys
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the commission to contract with private attorneys to collect and enforce defender liens and civil judgments.

headings.title: Attachment, service, and recording of lien claim
headings.reviewNote: Governs the timing of lien attachment against defendant assets upon filing, requiring service on asset holders or recording with the county recorder of deeds.

headings.title: Deposit of collections into defender fund
headings.reviewNote: Directs collected reimbursement moneys into the Legal Defense and Defender Fund for staff training and litigation expenses.

headings.title: Custody, deposit, and audit of fund moneys
headings.reviewNote: Designates the state treasurer as fund custodian, establishes deposit and interest crediting procedures, and requires state audits and bond protection.

headings.title: Fund disbursements and nonreversion of balances
headings.reviewNote: Directs the commissioner of administration to approve fund disbursements upon the director's request and exempts unexpended balances from general revenue transfer under section 33.080.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 7 subsection headings for 600.090 covering mandatory cash contributions and reimbursement, statutory defender liens and prosecutor enforcement, private collection contracts, lien attachment and recording, Legal Defense and Defender Fund creation, treasury custody and audit, and disbursements with section 33.080 nonreversion (L. 1976 H.B. 1095 § 600.053 through A.L. 2016 S.B. 735).
